description: Axiom-owned out-of-tree explicit spec (jrpc-errclass lane) for the error-code classification of nim-json-rpc's json_rpc/errors.nim::new: the constructor's case/if/else chain (errors.nim:105-122) maps every int error code to exactly one of eight concrete classes, and this adoption pins that mapping as a PRIORITY TABLE — first match in tag order wins (the five singleton codes from JSON-RPC 2.0 §5.1 take precedence over the reserved band [-32768, -32100] that contains them, exactly as the source's case arms precede the else chain), followed by the server band [-32099, -32000] and the application remainder, with class tags 0..7; the EFFECTIVE partition (accounting for priority) is exclusive and exhaustive. The ADOPTED MODEL is constructed IR (the mapping's irIf chain) — the subject body is deliberately NOT materialized (template err, obj-constr, move, and in-range membership are outside the certified extraction subset; the subject is never modified, Zero-Footprint). Thirteen INSTANCE obligations pin the boundary values (each: pre code == <c>, post result == <expected tag>); a confirmed counterexample is replayed against the ORIGINAL constructor through a stamped of-matrix harness that imports json_rpc/errors and observes the dynamic class as an int tag between the replay markers. The adoption record is HASH-BOUND: the loader recomputes the specification artifact's spec identity (SpecID = H(sorted canonicalSpecIR | origin | ruleVersion)) from the loaded proposition content and fails closed unless it byte-equals adoption.adoptedSpecHash, and adoption.subject.blobSha256 is verified against the actual module bytes under the run's subject root.

adoption.basis: adopted from the frozen soundness contract experiments/jrpc-errcode-slice-e2e/FREEZE.md (P0) and its P1 gate record (all three gates PASS — of-matrix observation 13/13, loader applicability, engine attachment points)
adoption.provenance: The mapping CONTENT (8 regions, 13 boundary instances, tag assignment) was authored from the JSON-RPC 2.0 Specification §5.1 text and a line-cited reading of json_rpc/errors.nim:105-122 at the pinned commit, cross-checked instance-by-instance against the actual constructor behavior by the P1 probe (13/13 observed == expected; experiments/jrpc-errcode-slice-e2e/P1-GATE.md). No human authored this file's byte content; the AUTHORITY for verifying against it is the explicit adoption act — this committed Axiom-owned overlay whose adoption record hash-binds the exact proposition content and the subject module bytes. Content authorship confers NO authority. Any post-adoption content, ruleVersion, or subject-byte change mechanically invalidates the adoption (loader fail-closed).

semanticCaveats: The mapping is an ADOPTED MODEL in constructed IR (the irIf chain over one BitVec64 parameter), not an extraction of the subject body: the solver verifies the model, and the stamped replay harness observes the ORIGINAL constructor — the model-to-subject correspondence is evidence-backed (P1 of-matrix probe 13/13), not formally extracted.

The replay observation is the int tag of the observed dynamic class, produced by the harness's of-matrix (7 leaf discriminants + the base discriminant): the base check folds CondTrue over new's return type (the domain precondition — P1-GATE); leafCount > 1 or a failed base check quits the harness (abnormal exit => replay unavailable); leafCount == 0 resolves to the base tag.

The 13 instances are INSTANCE obligations over pinned boundary inputs (the sidecar contract's instance-obligation precedent), not a universal theorem over the input space; the -32100/-32099 pair pins the generic/server band boundary and -32000 pins the spec's dual boundary (the table's explicit definition wins over the reserved-range reading).

Nim int is pointer-width signed; all pinned codes and both range endpoints are far from any overflow boundary, and the model's signed comparisons lower to bvsle over two's-complement literals consistently on both the SMT and the concrete-evaluation sides.

The class names are nim-json-rpc's INTERNAL implementation choice (the spec defines code semantics, not class hierarchy); mapping undefined reserved codes to the generic base (tag 6) is the implementation's choice, recorded here as adopted fact, not spec norm.
nonClaims: NOT a claim about the subject's field values, message text, or data payloads — obj-constr and field semantics are outside the certified subset; the tag projection says nothing about them
NOT a claim that the classification holds for any input outside the 13 pinned instances (INSTANCE obligations; the mapping table itself is solver-checked as the carrier body over the pinned pre)
NOT a claim that the subject body was extracted, translated, or verified (the carrier is constructed IR from this document's mapping; the subject connection is the stamped replay observation only)
NOT a claim that nim-json-rpc was modified or annotated in-tree (Zero-Footprint)

NOT a re-derivation of the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification text — the mapping's spec grounding (the five named codes, the server band, the reserved band, the application remainder) is the spec's own statement, adopted here by the explicit hash-bound act

NOT a general detection proof for wrong mappings — the negative control is the specific mutation scenario of the frozen experiment (instance 4 expected distorted; detection evidence is produced by the mutation test, not claimed universally)
